newsitem.title: JAPAN: Higher sales tax cuts April car sales in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Higher sales tax cuts April car sales in Japan.

text.p: A boost in Japan's sales tax on April 1 sharply cut into vehicle sales during the month, resulting in the first sales drop in eight months, an industry body said on Thursday.
Vehicle sales fell 12.7 percent in April from a year earlier to 326,975 units, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said.
Carmakers had previously said they did not expect to see much of an impact from the tax increase from three percent to five percent in April because of the high volume of backlog orders they held.
"They (carmakers) might have run out of the backlog orders already. We are a little worried about sales this month and in June," an association official told Reuters.
"April sales fell unexpectedly, contrary to carmakers' expectations," Nomura Research analyst Seiji Sugiura said.
"And they may continue to fall (on a year-on-year basis) because last year's sales were high," Sugiura added.

In March, Yoshifumi Tsuji, chairman of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association, said the full effect of the tax increase would be felt in May and June, and would reduce overall sales compared with the 1996/97 business year.
"I estimate that vehicle sales in the year to March 1998 at 5.29 million units, down about 4.9 percent from a year earlier," Sugiura said.

All major makers saw their sales fall in April, but Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, Suzuki Motor Corp and Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd gained, helped by demand for new recreational vehicles such as Daihatsu's Terios, Fuji Heavy's Forester and Suzuki's Wagon R Wide.
The Terios went on sale in April while the other two were launched in February.
But industry leader Toyota said it expects sales to bounce back soon.

"We expect overall domestic demand to recover soon as carmakers plan to introduce many new models this year. In addition, there is huge potential demand for replacing cars bought in the period of bubble economy in the late 1980s," a Toyota Motor Corp spokesman said.
In March, vehicle sales rose 12.4 percent to 830,864 units from a year earlier as consumers rushed to buy cars ahead of the sales tax increase.
